title: Agent Failure, Stop, and Recovery Card
summary: Design explicit exits and reconciliation for non-progress, tool failure, partial effects, timeouts, stale state, unsafe instructions, and unavailable humans.
prerequisites: A bounded run contract with observable state and postconditions
Named incident, data, security, and business recovery owners

accessibility.plainLanguageSummary: Stop new work, find what actually changed, restore a known-good state, and verify before resuming.
accessibility.nonColorCues: Incident phases are numbered detect, contain, reconcile, recover, verify, and learn.
accessibility.reducedMotionAlternative: Display the entire incident sequence as a static runbook.

sections.title: Declare failures before the run
paragraphs: Define completion, non-progress, repeated action, budget exhaustion, policy denial, malformed tool output, untrusted instructions, stale state, timeout, human unavailability, and postcondition mismatch. A loop that merely stops producing errors is not necessarily complete.

Distinguish failure before an effect, uncertain execution, confirmed partial effect, and confirmed completed effect. Retrying an uncertain write without an idempotency or reconciliation strategy can make the incident worse.

sections.title: Recover in a controlled order
paragraphs: First stop admission and revoke or pause tool authority. Preserve logs, approvals, request identifiers, checkpoints, and external-system evidence. Query the system of record to determine what happened instead of asking the model to remember.

Reconcile each effect, compensate or restore where authorized, verify postconditions independently, and require a human release decision before resuming. Update fixtures and controls from the failure without erasing the original evidence.

code.label: Agent failure and recovery record
code.code:
Task: [FAILED OR UNCERTAIN AGENT RUN]
Scope: [RUN, TOOLS, IDENTITIES, STATE, EXTERNAL EFFECTS, AND AFFECTED USERS]
Permissions: [INCIDENT READ, CONTAINMENT, COMPENSATION, RESTORE, AND RESUME AUTHORITY]
Evidence: [TIMELINE, REQUEST IDS, APPROVALS, TOOL RESULTS, SYSTEM-OF-RECORD STATE, AND GAPS]
Authority: [INCIDENT COMMANDER, SECURITY/DATA OWNER, BUSINESS OWNER, AND RESUME APPROVER]
Failure class: [BEFORE EFFECT | UNCERTAIN | PARTIAL | COMPLETE BUT INVALID]
Stop conditions: [NEW WORK, REPEATED EFFECT, EVIDENCE LOSS, OR UNAUTHORIZED RECOVERY]
Verification: [RECONCILE EVERY EFFECT AND INDEPENDENTLY CHECK RESTORED POSTCONDITIONS]
Recovery: [CONTAIN, REVOKE, RECONCILE, COMPENSATE/RESTORE, VERIFY, AND APPROVE RESUME]

sections.title: Expected evidence and verification
paragraphs: Expected evidence includes detection time, containment action, authority revocation, preserved trajectory, external-system reconciliation, recovery action, independent verification, residual impact, and accountable resume decision.

Exercise at least timeout-before-write, timeout-after-write, duplicate request, stale checkpoint, unavailable approver, and malicious tool-output cases. Stop if recovery depends on unverified model narration. Recover from systems of record and immutable evidence.
